lesson_title: Three Floors of Profit: the Statement of Comprehensive Income
hook_text: One page. Three floors. The whole year rides the lift down.
clip_script: The owner's mother visits and asks the only question that matters: 'So — how was the year?' You can't hand her a pile of journals. You need ONE page. Picture it as a building with three floors, and the year's money riding the lift down. Top floor: only two residents — what customers paid, and what the goods had cost. The difference: trading profit, R20 000. Is the pricing healthy? Middle floor: real life — wages, telephone, insurance, the missing stock. What survives: operating profit, R9 100. Is the shop as a machine healthy? Ground floor: the loan's interest takes its bite, and what walks out the front door is the net profit: R7 900. Why three floors instead of one big room? Because when something goes wrong, the floors tell you WHERE. Thin at the top: pricing problem. Thin in the middle: cost problem. Thin at the bottom: debt problem. One room hides the leak. Three floors point at it.
visual_style: A cutaway three-storey building with money riding a glass lift downward, amounts peeling off at each floor; a leak-detector torch highlighting each floor as the diagnoses are named.
pacing: Floor-by-floor descent with a beat per subtotal, snapping to the leak-location payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the page any reader can trust.
